newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian markets hope for post-Easter price hop.
newsitem.headline: Russian markets hope for post-Easter price hop.

text.p: Some Russian shares firmed though foreign investors stayed home on Friday, but traders said the snatch of buying was unlikely to lift the market next week.

Domestic-dominated treasury bills showed more holiday sparkle, though some traders said a half-percent average fall in yields was on hopes foreign investors would hop back into the post-Easter market with new allocations.
The Russian Trading System (RTS) 23-share index slipped 0.4 percent to 297.46 from 298.68. Volume was a miserly $16.8 million, of which $11.9 million was natural gas monopoly Gazprom.

Gazprom GAZP.RTS eased to $0.680 from $0.685 on active trade, including four reported afternoon deals for three million shares each and one in the morning. Only three other shares had reported trade over $1 million.

Foreign buyers have shunned Russian shares for the last couple of weeks, though few sellers have been seen, and operators, who did not speculate on the Gazprom activity, said they hoped the second quarter would see a new rally.
The RTS index has fallen about 15 percent since a high of 349.27 on February 20.

Market volume, which many dealers correlate with price trends, has fallen to around $20 million per day from around $40 million during the two-month new year rally which lifted the RTS index from 200.
Traders said that there was no evidence yet that a rally was readying.
"I have not seen a single deal by a foreign investor in the last few days," said Trinfiko dealer Grigory Pinsky.
United City Bank dealer Dmitry Yevenko said some investors expected a further 10 percent fall in the market before activity revived. "You cannot discount that opinion," he said.
Treasury bill dealers, who bid average yields down to 33.2 percent from 33.8 percent on 5.5 trillion roubles turnover, average for this market, also said April could see prices rise.
Tokobank dealer Mikhail Abrashin said yields could fall to 25-27 percent by the end of April thanks to new foreign funds.
"We will see a stream of non-resident funds at the beginning of April," he said.

The new Russian government cabinet, considered strongly reformist, and Central Bank rules making investment repatriation easier expected in April would cause a general re-rating of the domestic market, he said.
Mosbiznesbank dealer Dmitry Lukashov said the next Wednesday auction would indicate the short term trend by showing the strength of the Central Bank and Ministry of Finance.
"But even if yields go up, it won't be by much, since so many are ready to invest at current levels," he said.
